Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The resize listener, grid's dimension-change guard, native titlebar layout, and configuration inspection implementation establish the complete synchronous path. Built-in language extensions provide dozens of override groups; exact frame-time impact is unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous renderer CPU for nested configuration-override scans and deep-cloned override contents, plus temporary objects generating GC pressure.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For B effective consolidated override groups and I identifier occurrences, each inspection performs O(B*I) group checks plus cloning/merging matching contents; typical single-language groups give O(B^2). This repeats once per titlebar layout with changed dimensions, even with warm configuration caches.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased synchronous CPU and allocation before resize frames can complete, degrading resize responsiveness in configurations with many or large language overrides.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: getWindowControlsStyle read controlsStyle from the cached consolidated window configuration using getValue('window'); it did not enumerate or clone language overrides.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every call now constructs a configuration inspection and enumerates every consolidated language-override identifier, even when window.controlsStyle cannot have language overrides and the process is not a Snap.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The deleted cached getValue('window') lookup is replaced by unconditional inspect('window.controlsStyle') at line 447, before the Linux-Snap/Wayland condition. This adds override enumeration to existing layout calls on non-Snap Windows/Linux as well as Snap.
Findings.Title: Keep full configuration inspection off the non-Snap resize path
Findings.Impact: Resizing an ordinary non-Snap Windows/Linux window with a custom titlebar now pays collection-wide override scans and cloning on each width-changing layout. Built-in language defaults already supply dozens of groups, and additional language extensions/user overrides increase the cost despite having no relationship to the Snap-specific default.
Findings.Evidence: src/vs/workbench/electron-browser/window.ts:154 directly handles resize with layoutService.layout(); workbench/browser/layout.ts:1894 lays out the grid, whose gridview.ts:935-944 skips only unchanged dimensions. NativeTitlebarPart.layout at workbench/electron-browser/parts/titlebar/titlebarPart.ts:273-276 calls useWindowControlsOverlay, which calls getWindowControlsStyle at window.ts:479. Configuration.inspect in configurationModels.ts:837-848 loops all override identifiers and invokes getOverrideValue for each; getOverrideValue at 122-126 calls getContentsForOverrideIdentifer, which at 247-272 rescans all groups and deep-clones/merges the matching contents before discovering this setting is absent. This enumeration is not cached. Language defaults such as extensions/prompt-basics/package.json:108-170 and extensions/json-language-features/package.json:152-170 populate those groups.
Findings.Recommendation: Retain the getValue-based fast path outside Linux-Snap Wayland, and perform the explicit-configuration inspection only when needed for the Snap fallback. If the Snap decision is cached, invalidate it on relevant configuration changes rather than recomputing it during layout.

Scenarios.Scenario: Native Windows/Linux window creation, resizing, and titlebar styling, including non-Snap installations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resize directly calls workbench layout; changed-dimension grid leaves synchronously lay out the native titlebar. Window-controls configuration inspection must finish before titlebar layout returns and rendering can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: nativeHostService.updateWindowControls sends changed overlay height or colors to the native host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Height updates are deduplicated by cached height; styling uses the existing color condition. Snap Wayland custom controls skip these overlay operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same native-host operations and height deduplication; the controls-style decision used a cached getValue lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Inspection precedes the overlay decision even when cached geometry prevents an IPC update. IPC itself is not newly increased by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronously scan configuration override collections and clone/merge matching language contents before finding no window-controls override.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(B*I) group checks and matching-content copies per inspection, typically O(B^2); newly called from each dimension-changing native titlebar layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same decision performed getValue('window') against a cached consolidated model without override enumeration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on the renderer before layout and the resize frame can finish.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective consolidated language-override groups B and identifier occurrences I, including built-in extension defaults, installed extension defaults, and user/workspace overrides. Single-language groups commonly make I approximately B. Inspection repeats for each dimension-changing titlebar layout, not each editor row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous, serialized renderer-thread work. No debounce or worker offload at the new inspection. Each affected window has its own titlebar path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Consolidated configurations and unchanged grid dimensions are cached. However, each inspect call re-enumerates identifiers and getOverrideValue rescans and clones matching override contents even with warm caches and an absent window.controlsStyle override. Unchanged grid dimensions skip titlebar layout entirely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: complete resize-to-grid-to-titlebar-to-inspection call path and uncached nested scans/cloning were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame-time impact and prevalence of large language-override configurations are unmeasured. Built-in defaults already establish dozens of groups; uncertainty in magnitude is reflected in low severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one introduced repeated-work regression at window.ts:447. Custom-control DOM allocation is bounded per window and is not a separate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold, post-update, and warm Snap desktop/CLI/URL-handler launch on X11 or Wayland
Scenarios.CriticalPath: electron-launch performs environment setup and filesystem checks, starts cache-generation helpers when needed, waits for all helpers, then execs the existing code CLI wrapper and Electron. First-launch helper work is on the startup path, not detached from it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check runtime/socket/directory paths and optionally create one compatibility symlink; export graphics and PipeWire library directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Constant path checks and at most one symlink per invocation; warm existing socket/link paths avoid creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Already checked a parent runtime socket and optionally created one symlink; the new protocol handling adds bounded checks and two driver-directory checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Checks complete before the executable starts; no socket connection or PipeWire daemon launch is issued by these changed lines.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Rebuild GIO, schema, image-loader and GTK input-method caches using core24/staged helpers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one invocation per helper per cold/update launch, with schema work grouped across effective data directories; not one process per module/schema. Warm update-gated calls are absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same helper families, update guards, concurrency and join; the PR retargets core20/GTK paths to core24/t64 and stages additional module providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Jobs overlap, but their completion is joined before exec.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write the version marker, migrate the old cache if present, remove stale MIME data and rebuild symlink/cache directories on updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per applicable launch/update; file work scales with actual cache/module contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: MIME removal, migration, version-marker handling and cache directory ownership already existed; deleted MIME-generation code was commented out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Migration/MIME removal run before exec; cache jobs are joined.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Exec the code wrapper, which runs Electron as Node for the CLI and follows the existing launch flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One wrapper/CLI execution per launcher invocation, unchanged; removing forced X11 does not itself add processes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same wrapper execution with an unconditional --ozone-platform=x11 argument.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Launcher setup and helper joining precede this transition.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One launcher execution per invocation; constant environment-variable and socket checks; module/loaders counts and effective XDG data-directory/schema groups for cold cache generation. No workspace-file or editor-row fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most four existing cache-generation jobs run concurrently within one cold launcher, then wait_for_async_execs joins them. No new global launch coalescing; independent invocations remain independent as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing .last_revision marker keyed by SNAP_VERSION controls update work. Gdk-pixbuf also checks for a missing cache file. Warm launches skip the update-gated module/schema/input-method jobs. Expanded original-environment metadata is a fixed set of variables.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for bounded launch checks, helper cardinality and unchanged cache/join behavior; insufficient evidence for a GPU fallback or newly expensive native initialization regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual helper times, platform GPU-driver selection, and externally packaged module behavior were not measured. Packaged driver names alone do not prove software rendering or additional runtime processes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional high-confidence regression. The newly enabled Wayland behavior and bounded environment/socket handling do not independently establish scaling performance costs.

Scenarios.Scenario: Integrated/external terminal creation and revival after launching from Snap
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Build the terminal environment, sanitize/restore original values, merge terminal overrides, then invoke the existing terminal backend or spawn. Revival resolves each saved environment before sending the grouped revival request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read existing process/shell environments, revive terminal processes in a grouped backend request, restore layout and request terminal layout info.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Environment transformations scale with saved terminals; reviveTerminalProcesses remains one grouped call for the workspace's revival buffer, not one IPC per restored original variable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same environment reads and grouped revival, without the original-Snap-value restoration scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resolved environments must complete before grouped revival; the diff adds no asynchronous dependency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn the selected external terminal with a sanitized environment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One spawn per external-terminal request, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same process spawn following sanitation; Snap-mutated variables were previously left in the environment.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check /etc/debian_version to select a default terminal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing cached default selection; no new check per restored variable or terminal item from the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Default selection precedes external spawning when no executable is configured.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: E environment keys per created/revived terminal and T terminal launch configurations. The new sanitation adds a second O(E) scan and restores at most the launcher's fixed set of original-value keys.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sanitation is synchronous per environment. Revival already resolves saved entries with Promise.all and then makes one grouped reviveTerminalProcesses call. External spawning remains one process per requested external terminal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new sanitation cache or retained map. Original-marker keys are removed from the result. External default-terminal discovery already caches its promise; revival shares existing environment-service reads where provided by the backend.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: sanitation callers, terminal override ordering, grouped revival and external spawning were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Environment sizes and numbers of revived terminals vary. The added linear pass over normally small environments is bounded and does not prove consequential launch degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: bounded linear metadata restoration with no introduced process/IPC fan-out, retention or new await.

Scenarios.Scenario: Snap preparation, CI packaging, and installation/update payload
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Gulp prepares the package tree; the existing single Docker build performs apt setup, OpenSSL linking and Snapcraft packing. Stage-package acquisition, build/prime hooks and compression must finish before the artifact is copied/published. End-user install/update requires fetching the artifact and core24 if absent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the pinned build container, apt update/upgrade/install, existing OpenSSL link steps and Snapcraft pack in destructive mode.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One container invocation; fixed apt commands; two gcc calls per matching existing SDK prebuild; at most four Snapcraft attempts only for eligible early Store failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same container/build-script sequence and bounded retries, using an older pinned image and snapcraft snap rather than pack.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire core24 and the missing deduplicated stage dependencies, including newly requested graphics, input-method, media, icon/MIME and WebKit packages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One base snap if uncached; package retrieval per unique missing package/dependency within the existing code part. Warm actual cache hit counts are not available; no runtime download per library is implied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Already acquired core20 and the smaller declared dependency set; the diff adds dependencies and preserves icons in the artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Acquisition precedes packing; added payload also contributes to normal installation/update transfer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy package files, strip base-provided files from prime, retain newly packaged icons and write template substitutions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing full package copy and one rm subprocess per base-snap file/link; added substitutions and ELF patches are bounded, while extra staged files add ordinary packaging bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same copy and per-base-file removal structure against core20; icons were excluded and there were fewer fixed ELF patch commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preparation and prime cleanup complete before compression; these are not editor runtime operations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One Snap build per eligible x64 pipeline job; supported preparation targets are now x64/arm64. Downloads scale with the deduplicated union of stage-package dependencies missing from caches, not with workspace files or every Electron executable. Prime cleanup scales with base-snap files; added ELF patches are a fixed set plus existing Copilot prebuild matches.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One docker run and sequential build script per job. OpenSSL linking and patchelf hooks are sequential. The code part precedes cleanup. Retry attempts are serialized; the new failure-state find exits at the first entry.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Preparation continues to delete the architecture staging tree. Snapcraft/apt/image cache contents are external and not inspectable here; successful unique dependencies can be reused according to those existing mechanisms. Store retries remain at most four attempts with three bounded jittered backoffs and stop once part state or output appears.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for build sequencing, retry bounds and explicit additional staging; limited for external image/package internals.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Pinned container contents, actual dependency closure, artifact sizes and download/cache timings cannot be inspected with these source-only tools. Added declared packages establish added packaging work but not that required integration dependencies are unnecessary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional actionable regression: dependency/base migration intentionally changes payload, while existing per-file prime cleanup is not a newly introduced fan-out. The retry-state check is bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Snap CLI stdin import and extension temporary-resource downloads after TMPDIR relocation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Launcher now exports an absolute XDG_RUNTIME_DIR as TMPDIR. Native environment/tmpdir consumers choose temporary paths there. Stdin imports create a file and queue appends; extension downloadResource calls await the existing main-thread download before returning the URI.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Select a temporary path using os.tmpdir, create/chmod it and append decoded stdin chunks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file per piped import, with queued appends per incoming chunk; bytes proportional to input as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same queued file operations and bytes, using inherited TMPDIR or the platform default; the diff changes their backing directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: File creation precedes importing; queued writes track the existing stream lifecycle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request the existing main-thread resource download to a temporary URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per requested resource, unchanged; no extra request from TMPDIR restoration/export.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same request/await using an os.tmpdir-derived location outside the newly forced runtime directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Command awaits download completion before returning the temporary URI.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing temporary bytes grow with piped input/download size; one temporary file per import/download. No new copy, download request, retention owner or size transformation is added in these consumers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Stdin append operations use the existing Queue. Extension resource requests retain their existing RPC/async download concurrency; changing the target path adds no new issuance.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: TMPDIR selection is process environment, not a new cache. Temporary-file ownership and existing cleanup behavior are unchanged by the diff; host backing-store configuration is external.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that directory selection changes; insufficient evidence for a new retention/copy/fan-out mechanism or a specific host storage regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A runtime directory may have different memory/swap/storage characteristics from the inherited temp directory. Actual host mounts, large temporary workloads and a behavior-preserving narrower requirement for the relocation are not established from this repository; no backing-store performance claim was inferred solely from the environment variable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional high-confidence actionable finding; accounted for the relocated existing filesystem path without claiming new I/O cardinality or unbounded retention.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 10 changed files and every diff page against ddbdd50a9ed1f9dc32e4fbadcf950b290e7d35b4. Submitted one low-severity, high-confidence regression: uncached quadratic override inspection newly placed on dimension-changing native titlebar layouts. Traced Snap cold/warm launch, terminal spawning/revival, packaging/payload and temporary-file scenarios. No concrete removed performance regression qualified for blame/fix learning. Static read-only review; opaque container/dependency contents, native runtime behavior and timing measurements remain unavailable.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
